definitions.gloss: soot; black residue from incomplete combustion
definitions.explanation: The fine black particles that deposit on surfaces from smoke, especially from wood fires, candles, or exhaust. A common byproduct of traditional Japanese hearths and stoves.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天井|てんじょう}→天井：05008_tenjou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すす⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}いた→付く：01960_tsuku⟧。
⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{底|そこ}→底：12560_soko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧すす⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}→真っ黒：07614_makkuro⟧になった。
examples.english: The bottom of the pot turned completely black with soot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年末|ねんまつ}→年末：17688_nenmatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{家中|いえじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧すす⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{払|はら}って→払う：00535_harau⟧⟦{新年|しんねん}→新年：09787_shinnen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a custom of sweeping soot from the entire house at year's end to welcome the new year.

notes:
Written in kanji as {煤|すす}, but hiragana is the standard form in modern usage. Soot was a familiar substance in traditional Japanese homes that used ⟦{囲炉裏|いろり}→囲炉裏：12008_irori⟧ (open hearths) and {竈|かまど} (cooking stoves).

CULTURAL NOTE:
すす{払|はら}い (soot sweeping) is a traditional year-end cleaning custom, originally performed at temples and shrines on December 13th. It marks the beginning of preparations for the New Year.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- すす⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}く→付く：01960_tsuku⟧ — soot collects
- すす⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{払|はら}う→払う：00535_harau⟧ — to sweep away soot
- すす{払|はら}い — year-end soot sweeping (cleaning ritual)
- すす⟦だらけ→〜だらけ：18372_darake⟧ — covered in soot
- すすけた — sooty, smoke-stained

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{灰|はい}→灰：02244_hai⟧ — ash (the powdery residue left after combustion, as opposed to the black deposit)
- ⟦{煙|けむり}→煙：02705_kemuri⟧ — smoke (the airborne particles, not the deposited residue)
- ほこり — dust (general household dust, not from combustion)
